ideas.title: How many spikes can you hang
ideas.critique: This is the step that makes last session's post real. Before, spikes only came to the stone; now iron magnetises iron and each joint lets go by a law, so the chain is a real skill limit. Seen from outside, though, it is still 'stone picks up spikes, a few more this time', and only the sway and the dropped third spike will tell a viewer it is different.

ideas.title: Magnet fishing off the pier
ideas.critique: A rope, drag and buoyancy around the field solver give the stone a game you come back to, and each haul is different. The risk is the sea bed's iron: if it is placed by hand as a set of loot, the variety is typed in rather than earned.

ideas.title: Two metals in seawater bite the tongue
ideas.nearest: A wire that spins by itself
ideas.critique: A circuit solved by nodal analysis from what touches what is the big goal's backbone, and a creature's jolt is a strong moment to share. If the jolt and the raised feathers are a canned reaction to a threshold, the creature half of it is a puppet, and the score rests on how general the contact graph really is.

ideas.title: Green rock to a copper bead
same_form: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: This is the fourth 'a material is worked by heat or a tool and changes state, close up', and the glowing crucible is the hot glass picture again. Reduction done as temperature thresholds plus a charcoal check is a set of rules, not chemistry, though the copper is needed for the road.

ideas.title: Steer a cork boat with the stone
ideas.critique: Adding the gradient force to the floating needle is an honest step, and 'it goes where the pull is, not where you point' is a real lesson to learn by playing. But a reed course with a timer in a bowl is a small, expected mini game that stays in the bowl.

ideas.title: Lightning made the lodestone
ideas.critique: A fulgurite you dig out and spikes magnetised by a line current's field are a rare bit of physics to show. It is a weather event the player waits for rather than plays, and a branching glass path is easy to fake with a random walk.

ideas.title: A hedgehog of spikes
ideas.critique: Many magnetised bodies in balance, with contacts and repulsion, is harder and more visual than the chain. It uses the same stone and spikes in the same spot, and it only works if the spikes really find their own stance and do not snap onto placed slots.

ideas.title: Wind a coil with the beak
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: This is the big goal's core: turns counted by a real spindle, a field from the coil's own path, lifting by the soft iron solver, and Lumi's beak doing visible work. It needs a cell and wire that do not exist yet, so made this session the current is most likely a number typed in.

ideas.title: Find the buried stone
ideas.critique: A compass treasure hunt is the first game anyone would expect from a magnet and a compass. The physics is a damped needle in a superposed field, and the hunt is replayable but thin.

ideas.title: Black sand that stands up
ideas.critique: Thousands of grains on the GPU, bristling along field lines and dripping off, is something the island has never shown, and the field becomes visible without a single label. Drawing on the sand gives it a use, but the neighbour dipole sums in cells are where it will either hold up or turn into a look.
